summary: Explore our GIS Mapping and Spatial Analysis for Economics course. Gain essential skills to analyze spatial data and enhance economic decision-making.
lede: GIS mapping and spatial analysis for economics and business turns scattered business records into usable spatial evidence for market research, branch planning, logistics, and economic profiling. Using QGIS and structured workflows, you will prepare datasets, assign coordinates, analyse market areas, and communicate findings through maps, dashboards, scorecards, and executive-ready reports. You will practise geocoding, spatial joins, buffer analysis, thematic mapping, and site suitability scoring with QGIS, ODK, OpenStreetMap, and real business datasets. The training helps you identify demand, service gaps, catchment overlap, and expansion opportunities, then package reusable map packs, screening matrices, and spatial intelligence action plans for decision-makers.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work with business, economic, or operational data and now need to make it spatial. It is a strong fit if you support planning, market analysis, logistics, property, or investment decisions and want to produce location intelligence that stands up in reviews and client discussions.
audience: Operations Manager using location intelligence for service
modules: GIS mapping foundations for business decisions
prerequisites: You need a laptop capable of running desktop GIS software, a spreadsheet application, and a willingness to work with business and location datasets. Access to QGIS will be provided or confirmed before delivery, and any sample datasets used in exercises will be supplied during training.
